# Checkov check IDs held at ZERO failures on infra/ (the .tf scan in security.yml).
#
# THIS FILE IS THE GATE. `GATE_CHECKOV=block` fails the job when any check listed here
# reports a failure; every other Checkov finding is published and does not block. The
# reasoning — why an enforce list rather than a suppression list — is in
# .github/scripts/checkov-enforced.sh and docs/security-baseline.md.
#
# THE CRITERION IS "PASSES TODAY", NOT "MATTERS MOST". Every ID below was measured at zero
# failures against checkov 3.3.9 on 2026-08-09 (508 passed / 373 failed overall). Turning
# them on therefore cost no remediation, and the list needs no argument about relative
# importance — an argument that would have to be re-litigated every time someone added a
# resource. A couple are merely operational rather than security-critical (CKV_AWS_216,
# CKV_AWS_305); they are here because they pass, which is the whole rule.
#
# RE-MEASURED 2026-08-26, after the container platform landed: 918 passed / 736 failed, and
# the list went from 52 IDs to 89. Nothing was removed — every ID already here still measures
# zero — and the same rule produced the 37 additions: they pass, so they are enforced.
#
# THIRTY-FIVE of them came with the new VPC, ECS, ECR, ALB, ACM and API Gateway resources. TWO
# did not: CKV_AWS_251 and CKV_AWS_36 both evaluate the archive vault's CloudTrail, which landed
# on 2026-08-14 — five days after the 52-ID baseline — and had been passing, unenforced, ever
# since. Regenerate this list on any spec that adds a resource FAMILY, not only on one that adds
# six; those two sat outside the gate for twelve days because nothing did.
#
# The failing rules are NOT here, and each has a disposition in docs/security-baseline.md:
# no VPC, no CMK, no X-Ray, no WAF, and S3 versioning (deferred by decision — revisit
# before any real user data lands).
#
# TO REGENERATE after an intentional infra change:
#   checkov -d infra --framework terraform --skip-path .terraform --output json --compact \
#     --soft-fail > /tmp/ck.json
#   jq -r '(if type=="array" then .[0] else . end) |
#          ((.results.failed_checks // []) | map(.check_id) | unique) as $f |
#          ((.results.passed_checks // []) | map(.check_id) | unique)
#          | map(select(. as $c | $f | index($c) | not)) | .[]' /tmp/ck.json | sort
# Do NOT paste the output over this file unthinkingly: an ID that DISAPPEARS from it has
# started failing, and deleting the line is how a gate gets quietly turned off. Removing an
# entry is a decision that belongs in docs/security-baseline.md.
#
# Note: no --quiet above. It strips passed_checks, and the gate cannot tell "this check
# passed" from "this check never ran" without them.
#
# ENTRIES THAT ORDINARY WORK CAN TRIP, so the failure is recognised rather than mysterious:
#
#   * CKV_AWS_45 (no hard-coded secrets in a Lambda env) matches ANY 40-character run of
#     [A-Za-z0-9/+=] on shape alone — a slash-joined S3 prefix, a base64 value, or a 40-char
#     opaque id with no -, _, . or : in it. It is the one entry with a real false-positive
#     mode, and this gate has no per-finding suppression: the only lever is deleting the ID.
#   * A NEW BUCKET missing the usual block fires up to nine of these at once (CKV2_AWS_6,
#     CKV2_AWS_61, CKV_AWS_19, CKV_AWS_53-56, CKV2_AWS_65, CKV_AWS_300). That is the gate
#     working; add the public-access block, encryption and lifecycle rules.
#   * A NEW LAMBDA without `retention_in_days` on its log group trips CKV_AWS_66; a new SQS
#     queue without a CMK trips CKV_AWS_27/CKV2_AWS_73; a new state machine without
#     `logging_configuration` trips CKV_AWS_285; an `aws_lambda_permission` without
#     `source_arn` trips CKV_AWS_364.
#   * MANY IDs are evaluated against exactly ONE resource, and deleting that resource makes the
#     ID unevaluated — which is a hard error by design, so the line has to go in the SAME change.
#     Twelve were in that position before the container platform (CKV_AWS_41, 34, 70, 159, 216,
#     259, 305, 366 and CKV2_AWS_32, 46, 54, 72), and most of the 2026-08-26 additions join them:
#     every ECS, ECR and ALB entry except the three listener ones (CKV2_AWS_74, CKV_AWS_103 and
#     CKV_AWS_2, two apiece) has exactly one resource behind it — the count in each comment says
#     which. The first of the two known cases has now happened: the Cognito identity pool was
#     retired and CKV_AWS_366 left with it, in the same change. The second is next — retiring
#     CloudFront takes CKV2_AWS_32, 46, 54, 72, CKV_AWS_34, 216, 259 and 305 with it, and
#     CKV_AWS_70 has to be re-measured rather than reasoned about, because the distribution's
#     bucket policy is one of five and may or may not be that ID's only subject.

# aws
CKV_AWS_41     # Ensure no hard coded AWS access key and secret key exists in provider (1)
